activities.description: The highest peak in Karnataka at 1,930 meters, offering cloud walks, breezy western ghats ridges, and birthplace of Indian coffee cultivation.

activities.description: UNESCO World Heritage site representing the capital of the 14th-century Vijayanagara Empire. Marvel at the stone chariot, musical pillars, and Tungabhadra riverbanks.

activities.must_try_food: Traditional North Karnataka Jolada Rotti Oota (sorghum flatbread with brinjal curry).

activities.must_try_food: Dharwad Peda & Badami Shengachutney (peanut chutney powder) with Jolada Rotti.

activities.description: The second-highest plunge waterfall in India, where the Sharavathi river splits into Raja, Roarer, Rocket, and Rani cascades plunging 253 meters.
activities.cultural_note: Viewpoints maintained by Karnataka Tourism (KSTDC). Descent to the bottom involves 1,400 steps and may be restricted during high flow.

travel_notes: Opening hours: 7:30 AM - 6:00 PM (Laser light show at 7:15 PM).
Best experience: July to October (Peak monsoon flow).

responsible_tourism_tips: Footwear must be deposited outside sacred sanctums and heritage monuments.
Support local craftspersons at artisan markets and cooperative stalls.
Dispose waste responsibly and keep Karnataka's ghats and waterfalls pristine.
Speak politely with local drivers and shopkeepers using the survival Kannada phrases provided.
